title: What drove our portfolios this month
author: ACMIIL PMS Desk
excerpt: Strategy-wise commentary tied to the monthly factsheets — attribution, changes and outlook.
body: Indian equities spent much of the month consolidating after a strong run, with breadth narrowing as investors rotated toward earnings visibility over momentum. Against that backdrop, our portfolios held up on the strength of position quality rather than beta.
## What worked

Financialisation and capital-markets names continued to compound, helped by resilient credit growth and buoyant primary-market activity. Our manufacturing and infrastructure holdings also contributed as order books stayed healthy and margins expanded on operating leverage.
- Large-cap stability anchored drawdowns during the mid-month volatility
- Selective mid-caps in industrials drove the bulk of relative outperformance
- Cash was deployed into two positions where valuations finally met our margin-of-safety threshold
## What we trimmed

We pared exposure to a consumer name where the risk-reward had narrowed after a sharp re-rating, and exited a position on governance concerns flagged in our forensic review. Discipline on exit is as important as conviction on entry.
## Outlook

We remain constructive but valuation-aware. The structural story — India's march toward a larger, more formalised economy — is intact, and we would use any broad-based weakness to add to businesses that clear all four of our mandated pillars.

body: Our fund manager shared the desk's view on where disciplined, research-first investing finds opportunity in the current market — and why process, not personality, is what compounds over cycles.

title: Why GARP works across market cycles
author: ACMIIL PMS Desk
excerpt: Growth at a Reasonable Price is not a compromise — it is a discipline that keeps compounding when momentum fades.
body: Every few years the market rewards one style to the exclusion of others — deep value in a recovery, high-growth momentum in a liquidity-flush bull. Styles that work spectacularly in one regime often unwind just as fast in the next.

GARP — Growth at a Reasonable Price — is deliberately built to be less regime-dependent. It asks two questions of every business: is it genuinely growing, and are we paying a sensible price for that growth?
## The two questions, applied
- Growth must be structural, not cyclical — large addressable markets, pricing power and durable moats
- Price must offer a margin of safety — we anchor to forward cash flows, not to the last quarter's momentum
## Why it compounds

By refusing to overpay, GARP limits the drawdowns that quietly destroy long-run returns. And by insisting on real growth, it avoids the value traps that look cheap for a reason. The result is a portfolio that participates in up-markets without being fragile in down-markets.
It is not the flashiest approach in any single year. Over a full cycle, that is precisely the point.
